meaning: to avoid talking directly about the main subject
example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what happened.
origin: Probably from hunting, where beaters struck bushes to flush out birds rather than striking the bird itself

wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This takes the words literally; the idiom has nothing to do with gardening
The idiom refers to avoiding a topic, not to causing physical harm
This is the opposite of the idiom, which describes delaying the direct point

explanation: 'Beat around the bush' describes indirect talk that avoids the main point. Hunters once beat bushes to make birds fly out, so the phrase suggests going around the subject instead of addressing it directly.
